kf1.tip: Sketch scales weighing the war with Spain, Tyrone's rebellion, bad harvests and the deaths of Walsingham and Burghley against patronage, Gloriana, 1588 and Robert Cecil.
kf1.note: A good sketch puts the war with Spain, Tyrone's rebellion, the four bad harvests of 1594 to 1597 and the deaths of Walsingham (1590) and Burghley (1598) on one pan. Patronage, the Gloriana image, the legacy of 1588 and Robert Cecil go on the other. The scales must tip towards Elizabeth keeping her authority. A strong sketch also links pairs, such as Cecil taking on Burghley's administrative weight after 1598.

kf2.tip: Find the weakest link in this chain: Cecil warned in advance, Essex declared a traitor, royal heralds on the streets, Essex fails to rally support. Say why.
kf2.note: Most would pick the last link, heralds causing Essex's failure to rally support. Londoners did not join him, but his support was already draining after he lost the sweet wines monopoly in 1600, so the heralds were not the only cause. The first links are strong: informants warned Cecil, so he could declare Essex a traitor before the march. The trap is naming a link without saying what else could explain the result.

cs1.tip: Explain to a Year 7, in 30 words or fewer, why Elizabeth letting Essex's sweet wines monopoly lapse in October 1600 could push him towards rebellion.
cs1.note: The sweet wines money paid for Essex's household, agents, soldiers and followers. Without it his finances collapsed within months and his followers had nowhere to go, so he believed he would soon be ruined. A good Year 7 version might be: Essex lost the money that paid his supporters, so he feared ruin and turned to force. If you only said he was angry or upset, you missed the money link.
